title.value: CADet: Fully Self-Supervised Anomaly Detection With Contrastive Learning
title.justification: The paper introduces CADet, a novel method for out-of-distribution (OOD) detection using self-supervised contrastive learning.
title.quote: This work explores the use of self-supervised contrastive learning to the simultaneous detection of two types of OOD samples: unseen classes and adversarial perturbations. First, we pair self-supervised contrastive learning with the maximum mean discrepancy (MMD). This approach enables us to robustly test whether two independent sets of samples originate from the same distribution, and we demonstrate its effectiveness by discriminating between CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-10.1 with higher confidence than previous work.

extractions.description: The paper presents CADet, a method using self-supervised contrastive learning combined with maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) for anomaly detection. CADet is designed to identify out-of-distribution inputs, focusing on detecting unseen classes and adversarial perturbations without requiring labeled data or access to OOD samples.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on improving machine learning methods for anomaly detection in various contexts and not specifically targeted at climate or ecological sustainability.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: The problem is especially acute for high-dimensional problems like image classification. Models are typically trained in a close-world setting but inevitably faced with novel input classes when deployed in the real world. The impact can range from displeasing customer experience to dire consequences in the case of safety-critical applications such as autonomous driving or medical analysis.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not directly address issues related to climate change or ecological sustainability. Its main focus is on advancing machine learning techniques for anomaly detection, which could have applications in various fields but is not specifically aimed at sustainable development.
primary_category.quote: Handling out-of-distribution (OOD) samples has become a major stake in the real-world deployment of machine learning systems.

secondary_categories.justification: As the paper primarily deals with machine learning anomaly detection without specific alignment to climate or ecological aspects, secondary sustainable development categories are not applicable.
secondary_categories.quote: We propose a self-supervised contrastive method for anomaly detection (both unknown classes and adversarial attacks) inspired by MMD.

primary_sub_category.justification: There are no specific sub-categories related to climate or ecologically-oriented sustainable development tackled in this research paper.
primary_sub_category.quote: Anomaly detection methods generally rely on one of three types of statistics: features, logits, and softmax probabilities.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: No secondary sub-categories related to sustainable development emerge from the content of this paper.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Our work intersects with the MMD, label-based OOD detection, adversarial detection, and self-supervised contrastive learning literature.

applications.justification: The applications highlighted in the paper are related to advancing computer vision models' robustness rather than addressing sustainability issues.
applications.quote: Significantly, CADet is fully self-supervised and requires neither labels for in-distribution samples nor access to OOD examples.

new_primary_category.justification: Existing categories do not apply as the paper does not address sustainable development in any direct way.
new_primary_category.quote: Nothing in the paper indicates a need for a new sustainability-related category.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: Sub-categories do not apply here given the focus on technological advancements in anomaly detection outside a sustainability context.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: CADet outperforms existing adversarial detection methods in identifying adversarially perturbed samples on ImageNet.
